samples.summary: `SELF_CLOSE_RE` truncates a legitimate trailing `/` from an unquoted attribute value, silently rendering a different `src` than a browser would
samples.evidence: `const region = (match[1] ?? '').replace(SELF_CLOSE_RE, '')` with `SELF_CLOSE_RE = /\/\s*$/` cannot distinguish a self-closing slash from the last character of an unquoted value. For `` the region is ` src=https://example.com/`, the trailing `/` is stripped, and the emitted image points at `https://example.com` — while the HTML parser spec keeps `/` inside an unquoted attribute value (only `>` terminates it). The tag still validates and renders, so the wrong URL is emitted silently rather than declining. Restricting the strip to a slash preceded by whitespace (`/(?<=\s)\/\s*$/`) would match the intent stated in the comment.

samples.summary: Wall-clock assertion (`elapsed < 1000ms`) makes the new regression test timing-dependent on shared CI runners
samples.evidence: `expect(elapsed).toBeLessThan(1_000)` measures real time around `render()`; on a loaded runner a linear 100k-char render can still be scheduled away for over a second, producing a flaky failure unrelated to the regression. The `expect(html).not.toContain('<img')` assertion on line 154 carries the behavioural check on its own; the timing bound is the only flaky part.

verdict.reason: The code shape is as quoted (img-plugin.ts:151 slices state.src per `]*`, which cannot cross a `<`; the next `]*` immediately hits `<` and matches empty, required `>` fails; the region-absent branch fails on the space) — O(1) per candidate. (2) The finding's cost model for the slice is factually wrong: a two-arg `slice` with a result >= 13 chars produces a V8 SlicedString in O(1) (parent flattened at most once, amortized), `String::IsFlat()` is true for sliced strings so `String::Flatten` is a no-op, and the native regexp entry unwraps parent+offset instead of copying. That is the same property that lets markdown-it's own inline rules do `state.src.slice(state.pos)` at every `<` without being quadratic.
